import Mathlib

/-!
# Finite sums of morphisms into a group object, and their permutation symmetry

Milne's proof of the Albanese universal property (*Abelian Varieties* III.6
Proposition 6.1) begins with the sentence "clearly this is symmetric, and so it
factors through `C^{(g)}`", where "this" is the morphism

`C^g ⟶ A`,  `(P₁, …, P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)`

into an abelian variety `A`. This file supplies that morphism and — the actual
mathematical content of the word "clearly" — its invariance under permuting the
`g` factors.

## Main definitions

* `MonObj.foldSum` — for a monoid object `A` in a cartesian monoidal category,
  the product `f 0 * f 1 * ⋯ * f (n-1)` of a finite family of morphisms
  `f : Fin n → (X ⟶ A)`, defined by recursion on `n` with the empty product the
  unit `η[A]`.
* `MonObj.powSum` — the specialisation to the projections of an indexed product:
  the morphism `∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C) ⟶ A` given by
  `(P₁, …, P_n) ↦ φ(P₁) * ⋯ * φ(P_n)`.

## Main results

* `MonObj.foldSum_comp` — `foldSum` is natural in the source: precomposing every
  member of the family with `u : W ⟶ X` precomposes the fold.
* `MonObj.foldSum_swap` — for a **commutative** monoid object, transposing two
  adjacent members of the family leaves the fold unchanged.
* `MonObj.foldSum_perm` — for a commutative monoid object, the fold is invariant
  under an arbitrary permutation of the family: `foldSum n (f ∘ σ) = foldSum n f`.
* `MonObj.powSum_perm` — consequently `powSum` is `S_n`-symmetric: precomposing
  with the permutation automorphism of `∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)` induced by `σ`
  leaves `powSum` unchanged. This is the hypothesis that Milne's symmetric-power
  universal property consumes.

## Why adjacent transpositions

`foldSum` is defined by recursion on the *shape* `Fin (n+1) ≃ Fin n ⊕ {0}`, so
the one-step lemma that the recursion supports directly is the adjacent swap
(`foldSum_swap`). Arbitrary permutations follow because
`Equiv.Perm (Fin n)` is generated by adjacent transpositions
(`Equiv.Perm.mclosure_swap_castSucc_succ`), which is the induction actually run
in `foldSum_perm`.

## References

Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.6 Proposition 6.1, p. 104 (the symmetrisation
step); blueprint `lem:symmetric_product_av_map` in
`blueprint/src/chapters/Albanese_AlbaneseUP.tex`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe v u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace CategoryTheory.MonObj

variable {K : Type u} [Category.{v} K] [CartesianMonoidalCategory K]

/-- **The `n`-fold product of a family of morphisms into a monoid object.**
`foldSum n f = f 0 * f 1 * ⋯ * f (n-1)`, with the empty product the unit
`η[A]`. Written additively (`P₁ + ⋯ + P_n`) in the Albanese application, where
`A` is an abelian variety. -/
noncomputable def foldSum {A X : K} [MonObj A] :
    (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → (X ⟶ A)) → (X ⟶ A)
  | 0,     _ => toUnit X ≫ η[A]
  | (n+1), f => lift (f 0) (foldSum n (fun i => f i.succ)) ≫ μ[A]

@[simp]
theorem foldSum_zero {A X : K} [MonObj A] (f : Fin 0 → (X ⟶ A)) :
    foldSum 0 f = toUnit X ≫ η[A] := rfl

@[simp]
theorem foldSum_succ {A X : K} [MonObj A] (n : ℕ) (f : Fin (n + 1) → (X ⟶ A)) :
    foldSum (n + 1) f = lift (f 0) (foldSum n (fun i => f i.succ)) ≫ μ[A] := rfl

/-- **`foldSum` is natural in the source.** Precomposing every member of the
family with `u : W ⟶ X` precomposes the fold. -/
theorem foldSum_comp {A X W : K} [MonObj A] (u : W ⟶ X) :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → (X ⟶ A)), u ≫ foldSum n f = foldSum n (fun i => u ≫ f i)
  | 0, f => by simp [foldSum, Subsingleton.elim (u ≫ toUnit X) (toUnit W)]
  | (n + 1), f => by
      rw [foldSum_succ, foldSum_succ, ← Category.assoc, comp_lift]
      congr 2
      exact foldSum_comp u n (fun i => f i.succ)

end CategoryTheory.MonObj

import Mathlib

/-!
# The `g`-fold sum `C^g ⟶ A` and its permutation symmetry

Milne's proof of the Albanese universal property (*Abelian Varieties* III.6
Proposition 6.1) opens with "clearly this is symmetric, and so it factors
through `C^{(g)}`", where "this" is

`C^g ⟶ A`,  `(P₁, …, P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)`

for `φ : C ⟶ A` a morphism into an abelian variety. This file supplies that
morphism together with the content behind the word "clearly": its invariance
under permuting the `g` factors. It is the input that the universal property of
the symmetric power `Sym^g C` consumes.

## The mechanism: hom-sets into a group object are commutative monoids

The whole file rests on a Mathlib fact that makes the geometry evaporate. In a
cartesian monoidal category, `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/Mon.lean`
equips the hom-set `X ⟶ A` of a monoid object `A` with a `Monoid` structure
whose multiplication is *definitionally* `f * h = lift f h ≫ μ[A]`, and upgrades
it to a `CommMonoid` when `A` is a commutative monoid object (`IsCommMonObj`).
`Over (Spec k̄)` is cartesian monoidal and braided, and an abelian variety is a
commutative group object there.

So the `g`-fold sum is a `Finset.prod` of morphisms, its symmetry is
`Equiv.prod_comp`, and no hand-rolled induction over `Fin g` is needed. Stating
it this way is not a shortcut: it is the correct observation that Milne's
"clearly" is exactly the commutativity of `A`'s group law and nothing else.

## Main definitions

* `MonObj.powSum` — the morphism `∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C) ⟶ A` sending
  `(P₁, …, P_n) ↦ φ(P₁) * ⋯ * φ(P_n)`, i.e. the product over `i : Fin n` of the
  projections composed with `φ`.
* `MonObj.permAut` — the automorphism of `∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)` permuting the
  factors along `σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`.

## Main results

* `MonObj.powSum_perm` — **`powSum` is `S_n`-symmetric**:
  `permAut C σ ≫ powSum n φ = powSum n φ`. This is Milne's "clearly this is
  symmetric".
* `MonObj.comp_powSum` — `powSum` is natural in the source.
* `MonObj.permAut_one`, `MonObj.permAut_comp` — `permAut` is a monoid
  anti-homomorphism from `Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`, recording that the factor
  permutation is a genuine group action on `C^n`.

## References

Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.6 Proposition 6.1, p. 104; blueprint
`lem:symmetric_product_av_map` in
`blueprint/src/chapters/Albanese_AlbaneseUP.tex`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe v u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace CategoryTheory.MonObj

variable {K : Type u} [Category.{v} K] [CartesianMonoidalCategory K]

section PermAut

variable [HasFiniteProducts K]

/-- **The factor-permuting automorphism of `C^n`.** For `σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`,
the morphism `C^n ⟶ C^n` whose `i`-th component is the `σ i`-th projection; on
points, `(P₁, …, P_n) ↦ (P_{σ 1}, …, P_{σ n})`. -/
noncomputable def permAut (C : K) {n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) :=
  Pi.lift (fun i => Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) (σ i))

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
theorem permAut_π (C : K) {n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (i : Fin n) :
    permAut C σ ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i = Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) (σ i) := by
  simp [permAut]

@[simp]
theorem permAut_one (C : K) (n : ℕ) : permAut C (1 : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) = 𝟙 _ := by
  apply limit.hom_ext; intro i; simpa using permAut_π C 1 i.as

/-- Permuting by `σ` and then by `τ` is permuting by `σ * τ`. (The order records
that `permAut` is contravariant: it permutes *coordinates*, not indices.) -/
@[simp]
theorem permAut_comp (C : K) {n : ℕ} (σ τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    permAut C σ ≫ permAut C τ = permAut C (τ * σ) := by
  apply limit.hom_ext; intro i
  simp [permAut, Category.assoc]

end PermAut

section PowSum

variable [HasFiniteProducts K] [BraidedCategory K]

/-- **The `n`-fold sum morphism `C^n ⟶ A`.** For `φ : C ⟶ A` into a commutative
group object, the morphism sending `(P₁, …, P_n) ↦ φ(P₁) * ⋯ * φ(P_n)`, formed as
the product in the commutative monoid `(C^n ⟶ A)` of the projections composed
with `φ`.

In the Albanese application `A` is an abelian variety and the group law is
written additively: this is `(P₁, …, P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)`. -/
noncomputable def powSum {C A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] (n : ℕ) (φ : C ⟶ A) :
    (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ A :=
  ∏ i, (Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ)

/-- **Milne's "clearly this is symmetric".** The `n`-fold sum is invariant under
permuting the factors of `C^n`. The proof is exactly the commutativity of the
group law of `A`: in the *commutative* monoid `(C^n ⟶ A)` a finite product is
invariant under reindexing (`Equiv.prod_comp`).

This is the hypothesis consumed by the universal property of the symmetric power
`Sym^n C`, which is what licenses the factorisation `C^n ⟶ Sym^n C ⟶ A`. -/
theorem powSum_perm {C A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] (n : ℕ) (φ : C ⟶ A)
    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    permAut C σ ≫ powSum n φ = powSum n φ := by
  classical
  rw [powSum, Finset.comp_prod_eq_prod_comp_left]
  · -- Reindexing a finite product in a commutative monoid along `σ`.
    calc ∏ i, (permAut C σ ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ)
        = ∏ i, (Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) (σ i) ≫ φ) := by
          refine Finset.prod_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
          rw [← Category.assoc, permAut_π]
      _ = ∏ i, (Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ) :=
          Equiv.prod_comp σ (fun i => Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ)
  · exact fun _ _ => Hom.comp_mul _ _ _
  · exact Hom.comp_one _

/-- `powSum` is natural in the source: precomposition distributes over the sum. -/
theorem comp_powSum {C A W : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] (n : ℕ) (φ : C ⟶ A)
    (u : W ⟶ (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C))) :
    u ≫ powSum n φ = ∏ i, (u ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ) := by
  classical
  rw [powSum, Finset.comp_prod_eq_prod_comp_left]
  · exact Finset.prod_congr rfl fun i _ => by rw [Category.assoc]
  · exact fun _ _ => Hom.comp_mul _ _ _
  · exact Hom.comp_one _

end PowSum

end CategoryTheory.MonObj
